added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite or after_suite arm, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: follow-on: the Measure paragraph labels the head arm "change present, revision 91a8aea54", which is the base revision, while the head-gate.log it cites carries "arm=head revision=58efccfe838c7a0bb506072abdc06264cc2e09ca" on its first line, so the fragment states a head-arm revision its own cited capture contradicts.

follow-on: the sibling reader of the same capability, _LOGGED_REVISION_RE via recorded_log_revision at review.py:1704, is still case- and label-sensitive — it returns None for "REV=<sha>", "Revision: <sha>" and "rev=<sha>" (measured at head) — so a log the audit now accepts annotates with a null head_log_revision and the two readers of one first-line revision disagree.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 91a8aea54aca17e98ce06aa7d3012bfe361105ef; one commit (58efccfe838c) changes three files — reports.py (the pattern plus its comment), the new test file, and the new evidence fragment — all inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_a_revision_label_is_read_in_any_case.py; the manifest records the gate as 5 passed / EXIT=0 at head-gate.log and the run directory negative-control.log as 3 failed, 2 passed / EXIT=1, and I re-ran the single named test at head (58efccfe838c) and got 5 passed.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is "Make the gate-log audit read a first-line revision label in any case while still requiring the label"; reckon/crew/reports.py:1146 recompiles _GATE_LOG_REVISION with re.IGNORECASE at reports.py:1148, so a first line reading REV=<sha>, Revision: <sha> or rev=<sha> is read while the label itself stays required.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits 58efccfe838c, tests and both logs recorded with their EXIT lines, but it carries no baseline_suite or after_suite arm, so the added-failure delta was not measured from suite logs.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's declared paths (reckon/crew/reports.py, tests/test_a_revision_label_is_read_in_any_case.py, the the-suite-is-green-at-head fragment, the a-revision-label-is-read-in-any-case figure directory); all three files in the diff are inside them.

justifications.durability: the three upper-case label cases parametrised at tests/test_a_revision_label_is_read_in_any_case.py:75 redden at the base tree in negative-control.log (REV=, Revision: and REVISION= fail there), so the assertion at :99 fails if re.IGNORECASE is dropped.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_a_revision_label_is_read_in_any_case.py is named by the done_when and its 5 passed / EXIT=0 head result is recorded in head-gate.log while negative-control.log records 3 failed / EXIT=1, and the ruff delta the fragment claims (one pre-existing SIM102 at reports.py:702) I reproduced at head.
justifications.fit: the re.IGNORECASE flag matches the sibling idiom _TEST_LOG_COMMAND_LABEL at reports.py:1227, and the added comment at reports.py:1141 describes the mechanism with no plan or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/reports.py:1148 adds re.IGNORECASE to _GATE_LOG_REVISION and the label requirement at reports.py:1147 is unchanged, so a bare hex run still names no revision.
justifications.reuse: no definition was added; the fix extends the single owner of the audit's first-line revision read at reports.py:1146, though a second reader of the same capability at review.py:1336 was left case-sensitive (see the finding).
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff touches only reckon/crew/reports.py, tests/test_a_revision_label_is_read_in_any_case.py and the fragment, every one inside the declared write paths.
